CaptureMode.description: How row-change events are captured for one database.

oneOf.description: Classify the SQL this worker executes. Writes from other clients are invisible. Works on every driver. The default.

Capture writes from any client, including other processes. Table-scoped bindings only. Postgres: triggers + LISTEN/NOTIFY on a dedicated connection (needs DDL rights). File-backed sqlite: triggers + changelog table + filesystem watch. MySQL: the binlog replication stream (needs replication grants, nothing installed).

DatabaseConfig.description: Per-database connection settings: either a connection `url` (whose scheme selects the driver) or the structured form (`driver`, `host`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `database`) — never both. `pool` and `tls` are optional and default when omitted.

capture.description: How `database::on-row-changed` events are captured for this database. `statements` (default) classifies the SQL this worker executes; `native` makes writes from ANY client — psql, other processes — fire too. Postgres: triggers + LISTEN/NOTIFY. File-backed sqlite: a trigger-fed changelog drained on filesystem wake-up. MySQL: the binlog replication stream (needs REPLICATION SLAVE + CLIENT).

database.description: Structured form: database name (postgres/mysql), or the database file path on the engine host (sqlite; `:memory:` for an in-memory one).

display.description: How clients draw this connection (icon, color). Metadata only.

driver.description: Structured form: the driver. Mutually exclusive with `url`.

folder.description: Absolute path of a folder on the engine host that holds this connection's `.sql` query files. Metadata only: the worker never reads it.

host.description: Structured form (postgres/mysql): server host name or IP. Through an `ssh` tunnel, the host as the SSH server resolves it.

password.description: Structured form (postgres/mysql): password — a literal, `secret://NAME` (the secrets worker's vault) or `env://NAME` (an environment variable the secrets worker reads). Resolved through `secrets::resolve`; never echoed back.

ssh.description: Reach the server through an SSH tunnel (postgres/mysql).

url.description: Connection URL. Driver is inferred from the scheme: `sqlite:`, `postgres://` or `postgresql://`, or `mysql://`. Mutually exclusive with the structured form (`driver` and its fields).

DisplayConfig.description: How a client draws a connection. The worker only stores it.

acquire_timeout_ms.description: Fail pool acquisition when no connection is available within this many milliseconds (1 ms to 10 min).

idle_timeout_ms.description: Close idle connections after this many milliseconds (at most 24 h).

max.description: Maximum number of open connections in the pool (1-500).

SshConfig.description: SSH tunnel to the database server (postgres/mysql): the worker connects to `host:port` as `user` and forwards each database connection through a `direct-tcpip` channel to the entry's host/port as the SSH server sees them. TLS to the database still verifies the database host name.

host.description: SSH server host name or IP.

host_key.description: Pin the server's host key by its OpenSSH SHA-256 fingerprint (`SHA256:…`, as `ssh-keygen -lf` prints it). A different key is refused. When absent, any key is accepted and `testConnection` reports the one it saw so a client can pin it.

passphrase.description: Passphrase of an encrypted `private_key` — a literal, `secret://NAME` or `env://NAME`.

private_key.description: Private key authentication: the key itself (OpenSSH or PEM; RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519), a path to it on the engine host, `secret://NAME` or `env://NAME`. Tried before the password when both are set.

TlsConfig.description:
TLS settings for a single database. Applies to postgres and mysql. Sqlite is local-file and ignores this block.

Default is `mode: require` — TLS handshake required, certificate chain validated against the system trust store, hostname verification skipped (matching libpq's `sslmode=require` semantics). Use `mode: verify-full` to additionally verify the certificate hostname matches the server host, and `mode: disable` to opt out of TLS entirely (local-dev only).

ca_cert.description: Optional CA certificate(s): a path to a PEM file, the PEM itself, `secret://NAME` or `env://NAME`. Additive by default — these certs **extend** the system trust store rather than replace it. Set `trust_native: false` for strict-isolation deployments that must only trust the operator-supplied bundle.

client_cert.description: Client certificate (chain) for mutual TLS: a path, the PEM itself, `secret://NAME` or `env://NAME`. Requires `client_key`.

client_key.description: Private key of `client_cert` (PEM: PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1): a path, the PEM itself, `secret://NAME` or `env://NAME`.

mode.description: TLS mode: `disable` (plaintext), `prefer` (TLS when the server offers it), `require` (default), `verify-ca`, or `verify-full`.

trust_native.description:
When true (default), the system/native trust store is loaded in addition to any `ca_cert` bundle. Set to `false` to trust only the `ca_cert` certificates — useful when an operator wants to pin trust to a private CA and explicitly *not* accept the public web PKI.

Effective for postgres. MySQL is forced-additive: `mysql_async`'s rustls path always loads the Mozilla `webpki_roots` bundle and extends it with `ca_cert` — there is no upstream knob to suppress the bundled roots, so `trust_native: false` only affects postgres.

Note: with both `trust_native: false` *and* `ca_cert: None` on postgres, no trust roots are available; pool construction fails with `CONFIG_ERROR`.

oneOf.description: No TLS. Plaintext connection. Local-dev only.
TLS when the server offers it (chain validated like `require`); plaintext only when the server does not offer TLS at all. A failed certificate check is an error, never a fallback.
TLS handshake required; certificate chain validated; hostname NOT verified. Matches libpq's `sslmode=require`. The default.
Same checks as `require` (chain validated against the trust roots, hostname not checked), named after libpq's `sslmode=verify-ca`.
TLS handshake required; certificate chain validated; certificate hostname must match the server host. Matches libpq's `sslmode=verify-full`.

description: Top-level worker config registered with the `configuration` worker.

databases.description: Named connection pools. Keys are logical database names referenced by RPC handlers (for example `primary`). At least one entry is required.

history_max_bytes.description: Maximum JSON-serialized size in bytes of one database's stored query history; oldest entries are dropped until the list fits. The hard guard that keeps history from growing into a value large enough to break the `state` worker's connection. `0` disables history recording. Applied live.

history_max_entries.description: Maximum entries kept per database in the console query history (`database::history`, stored on the `state` worker). Oldest entries are dropped first. `0` disables history recording. Applied live.
